paragraphs: Photos from the Small Zoo, posted by Mia. On Saturday, the Explorers went to the small zoo. I took all the photos myself, and Lily checked my words. A caption is a few words under a photo. It must describe the picture with the best words. Which caption do you like best?

Photo one is a picture of a camel. The camel stood in the sun and ate green leaves from a tree. It was as tall as a small bus. It was very heavy, but it moved slowly and quietly. Its neck was long, and its feet were wide. My first caption was "Camel." Lily said, "That is too short." So my second caption was "A tall camel eats green leaves in the sun."

Photo two shows a woman from the zoo. She was dressed in a green shirt and brown boots. She carried two big bottles of water to a bowl next to the camel. She filled the bowl with water. The camel put its head into the bowl and began to drink. "A camel can drink a lot of water," said the woman. My caption was "The woman fills the bowl, and the camel drinks."

Photo three shows Leo with his mouth open. He was amazed, because the camel put its face very near to him. Leo said, "It has very long eyelashes!" My caption was "Leo is amazed by the camel's long eyelashes." Lily said, "Good! The word amazed is better than the word happy." "It tells everybody how Leo feels." "A good caption says who is in the photo, and it says what happens," said Lily. "It also has one good word, like amazed," I said. We checked all three captions two times.

Here are my three captions on the page. Photo one: "A tall camel eats green leaves in the sun." Photo two: "The woman fills the bowl, and the camel drinks." Photo three: "Leo is amazed by the camel's long eyelashes." Leo laughed and said, "I like photo three the most!" Which photo do you like?
text.summary: Mia writes a photo page for Explorers' Blog about a visit to the small zoo. She shows three photos, and each photo has a short caption with the best words for the picture.
